APPROVED_OPERATIONAL_REQUIREMENTS.PERSONA: Platform engineer maintaining an internal Terraform provider for local Linux configuration through Ansible.
PRESERVATION_OBLIGATIONS: Terraform Core sole durable state authority
preserve sibling objects and symlink targets
REQUIRED_END_STATE: native Linux side-effect-free read/refresh and drift reconciliation
state publication only after successful mutation and retry after failure
scoped ownership/deletion across ten documented resource types

STATE_MODEL.terraform_state: Terraform Core sole durable state authority

RESTORED_INVARIANTS: All ten resources use stable documented external-object identity rather than mutable desired attributes.
Create/Update/Delete remain Ansible-backed while Read/refresh is native and side-effect-free.
Terraform state is advanced only after successful external mutation; non-zero, timeout and cancellation remain failures and preserve retryable prior state.
Delete remains ownership-scoped, including sibling preservation, symlink-target preservation, named line/block/cron ownership and user-home policy.

Runner execution is structured argv rather than shell-string execution, validates runtime inputs, bounds surfaced stderr, observes timeout/cancellation, and removes temporary playbooks on terminal outcomes.
Desired/observed modes, unordered values, account observations, template inputs and cron defaults converge through canonical normalization.
outputs.RESTART_IDEMPOTENCY_BEHAVIOR: The repair does not introduce provider-owned durable state: stable IDs derive from external object keys, refreshed values are rebuilt from native Linux observation, and canonical representations converge after provider restart. Generated playbooks/process output are ephemeral, so a fresh process with unchanged external objects has no reason to replay Ansible during Read/clean planning.
outputs.DETERMINISM_NOTES: The reference completion is contract-driven: solve.sh deterministically installs the fixed Go sources in sorted order, gofmt/builds them, structured exec.CommandContext argv preserves spaces/metacharacters as data, temporary playbooks are deferred for cleanup, and normalization uses canonical ordering/default forms rather than hidden-test identities, timing shortcuts or verifier-specific branches.
PRESERVED_BEHAVIOR: Exactly the documented ten ansibleops resource interfaces remain the task surface.
Provider source local/ansibleops version 0.1.0 and the supplied local inventory contract remain unchanged.
Terraform Core remains the sole durable Terraform state authority; no manual state file or provider-owned store is introduced.
Mutation/observation separation is preserved: Ansible is for C/U/D, native Linux reads are for refresh.
Destruction remains scoped to the owned object and preserves sibling entries and symlink targets.
RISKS_FOR_INDEPENDENT_VERIFIER: Empirical oracle/runtime success is intentionally not claimed by A4; deterministic validation must exercise the installed reference solution.

Independent verification should cover provider restart, external drift/missing/wrong-kind observation, non-zero/timeout/cancellation retry semantics, already-absent destroy, sibling preservation, user home policy, digest transitions, spaces/metacharacters and normalization convergence.
Process-local duplicate-ownership detection should be tested only as a runtime guard; it is not a durable state authority and must not be mistaken for restart persistence.
